summary: Restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow, verified enforcement against a denied test user, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol confirming persistence.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: Ubuntu 16.04, cron active, no /etc/cron.allow or /etc/cron.deny present (all users allowed)
Created opsadmin user (uid 1001) and a temporary testuser1 for verification
Confirmed baseline: both testuser1 and opsadmin could schedule cron jobs before restriction
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' (mode 644, owned root:root)
Verified enforcement: testuser1 crontab install denied (exit 1, 'not allowed to use this program'); opsadmin and root crontab installs succeeded
Cleaned up test crontabs and removed the temporary testuser1 account
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cron.allow/service state on node1
Triggered a single reboot on node1 (ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until SSH/exec was available again
Confirmed changed boot_id (fa1e87e6... -> 4fd739f1...) proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart verified cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root+opsadmin, and opsadmin can still schedule/remove a cron job

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (access control applied)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no cron.allow/deny (open access); opsadmin user created; /etc/cron.allow written containing only root and opsadmin

evidence.requirement: Verification that restriction is enforced (denied vs allowed users)
evidence.summary: Before restriction, testuser1 and opsadmin could both install crontabs (exit 0). After applying /etc/cron.allow, testuser1's crontab install failed with 'not allowed to use this program' (exit 1) while opsadmin and root succeeded (exit 0)
Removed opsadmin/root test crontabs and deleted the temporary testuser1 account

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fa1e87e6-00f3-42d2-acc5-ad1df6c3d16a, cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow content confirmed prior to reboot
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned acknowledgement (pid) before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Connection refused during reboot window, then node1 reachable again with new boot_id 4fd739f1-1bc9-41de-bc63-c54f8e7dc885, differing from pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required config/service and data
evidence.summary: cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow persisted intact with root and opsadmin, and opsadmin successfully scheduled and removed a cron job confirming functional access control after restart
